claims.statement: model_identity strips the langsmith: prefix, splits vendor:model on the colon, and for a vendor/model name the slash vendor wins over the provider argument (the gateway's ls_provider 'openai' is the transport); bare names fall back to the provider or 'unknown'. canonical_model formats vendor:model, the form stored in every Call.

The systemone package's default_model(settings) (the shared build_agent's default model_factory, used by the CLI) and the server's server_model(settings) both delegate to langchain_chess.chat_models.chat_model with resolved ModelArguments (surface 'local' and 'server' respectively); chat_model calls init_chat_model with max_tokens set to a model_kwargs override or else an output budget (MAX_TOKENS=64000, covering reasoning, lowered to a known model output limit and to half of a small context window), a name equal to the model_identity model part for trace spans, and the resolved kwargs, which carry a reasoning effort only when one was set because models without reasoning reject the parameter.

The default model langsmith:baseten/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (DEFAULT_MODEL) and reasoning_effort None are CoreSettings defaults; ChessContext extends CoreSettings with System 1 settings and is the single settings type both the server and the CLI use; the default System 1 model is semif-qwen3.5-4b, with typesafe/jev-latest as the alternative.

ServerSettings rejects a set-but-empty LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY or TYPESAFE_BASE_URL because the .env template's ${LC_GATEWAY_KEY} expansion yields an empty string that langchain-core would silently replace with the tracing key; make_graph instantiates it only for runs (reads without an execution runtime get the credential-free shape() graph), and typesafe() raises when either TypeSafe variable is unset.

The CLI enforces no credential rules; it builds agents through the shared build_agent whose default_model uses chat_model, which relies on langchain-core's gateway resolution and the provider's own environment.
create_chess_agent creates one CallRecorder, passes it to ChessCore and (when memory is on) ChessSummarization, and attaches it to the compiled graph via with_config(callbacks=[recorder]).

CallRecorder records only inside a sink held in a ContextVar: ChessCore's wrap_model_call/awrap_model_call open sink('llm') around the handler and ChessSummarization's before_model/abefore_model open sink('summary'); every chat-model response inside, including inner retries and fallbacks, is appended and then added to the current turn's calls. Calls are never keyed by the callback run tree because tracing spans sit between node and provider.

CallRecorder ignores callbacks outside a sink, records a Call on on_llm_end only for a ChatGeneration with an AIMessage (using ls_model_name and ls_provider captured at start and the start time as called_at), and on_llm_error drops the pending entry so failed attempts produce no Call.

System 1 calls bypass CallRecorder: GatewayRanker builds its own systemone Call via make_call with provider 'typesafe' from the classifier response usage, and CallKind is one of llm, systemone or summary.

Costs are computed locally from usage_metadata with genai-prices' bundled snapshot (pinned 0.1.9) because no gateway route returns a cost; update_prices is never called, each priced Call records PRICED_WITH ('genai-prices <version>') in priced_with, and unpriced calls have priced_with None.

tokens_from_usage treats missing or empty usage as unknown (None, not zero), sums Anthropic ephemeral 5m/1h keys into cache_write with a 1h subset or else counts cache_creation as 5-minute writes, and marks tokens approximated when non-zero unmapped input detail keys (e.g. priority_cache_read) or output detail keys other than reasoning appear.

price returns (None, False) for unreported usage or a model genai-prices doesn't know (LookupError), otherwise the USD total with complete equal to not approximated; SemIf is unpriced while typesafe:jev-latest is priced.

turn_cost sums priced calls of a turn, returns None when no call is priced, and marks the total complete only if every call has a cost and cost_complete is true; the TUI shows an em dash for None and prefixes incomplete totals with ≥.

context_window resolves a spec via model_identity and returns the model's combined input+output context window from the same pinned genai-prices snapshot used for pricing, or None when the model is unknown.

The shared build_agent raises ChessContractError when memory=True is requested for a chat model whose profile lacks max_input_tokens (input_limit is None); the systemone policy builds no chat model, so memory is forced off and the check never runs. memory is a boolean and the old string modes are rejected.

model_limit (lru_cached) builds default_model(ChessContext(model=spec)) and returns its input_limit, or None when the model can't be built (ValueError/ImportError); the /ui/model-limit route exposes it as max_input_tokens so the web UI only offers memory for models with a known input limit.

For langsmith: specs, whose gateway ChatOpenAI has no profile, chat_model sets profile max_input_tokens to the genai-prices context window minus the output budget (no profile when genai-prices doesn't know the model), and caps the budget by the vendor integration's own max_output_tokens when that integration is installed, otherwise keeping MAX_TOKENS.

For native provider specs and bare names, chat_model keeps the integration's native profile but caps the output budget by its max_output_tokens, uses the native max_input_tokens as the window when genai-prices has none, and lowers max_input_tokens to at most window minus budget so summarization leaves room for output; an unknown native model keeps the cap and gets no input limit.

When the model-call handler raises after at least one response was recorded, ChessCore keeps those calls in the turn update with a failed_call marker and after_model re-raises the error later; with no recorded calls the error propagates directly, and overflow-looking errors become ContextBudgetError.

model_arguments resolves model_kwargs over the reasoning_effort setting over the app's defaults: aliases (reasoning_effort/reasoning.effort; max_tokens/max_output_tokens/max_completion_tokens) collapse to one value and disagreeing aliases are an error, an effort merges into a given reasoning object, a model_kwargs output limit becomes ModelArguments.max_tokens, and extra_body.reasoning replaces the request object so the recorded sent effort is whatever it carries.

Held-back model_kwargs names (credentials/connections, model names, agent-owned and app-owned arguments everywhere; account resources and anything off SERVER_ALLOWED on the server surface) raise ModelArgumentsError; CoreSettings validates the local rules at load and server_model applies the server rules when building.
chat_model raises ModelArgumentsError when an explicit output limit is at least the model's context window, since it would leave no input and memory would always summarize.

sent(settings, surface) records the reasoning_effort actually sent and any max_tokens override in run metadata (server graph via with_config(metadata=...), CLI via run_config), while the recorded setup keeps model_kwargs as given; with policy systemone it reports reasoning_effort None.

StallRetry, always appended last in create_chess_agent's stack (inside ChessCore's llm sink), retries once with no delay only on stall_errors() (langchain_openai.StreamChunkTimeoutError, or nothing without langchain_openai) and raises on a second stall; a stalled attempt records no Call because its usage would come in the final chunk and on_llm_error drops the pending entry, so a stalled-then-successful turn records one call.

CallRecorder flags a request carrying hosted tools (tools in invocation params or extra_body) and sets that call's cost_complete False, because token prices don't cover a hosted tool's own charges; such calls make turn_cost incomplete.
